The most quarrelsome is most hated by Allah; the Prophet, being human, may mistakenly rule for the more eloquent party, and what is wrongly given is a portion of Fire.
In a dispute about land the Prophet ruled that seven cubits be left as a public way.
Umar says that since revelation has ended people are judged by their public deeds, their secrets left to Allah.
The Prophet may rule for the more persuasive party, but whatever is wrongly given that way is a piece of fire not to be taken.
When an Ansari disputing water claimed the Prophet favoured his cousin Az-Zubair, the Prophet gave Az-Zubair his full right; Az-Zubair linked the verse on making the Prophet judge.
The Prophet, only human, judges by what he hears, so whoever is wrongly awarded his brother's right by an eloquent case is given only a piece of Fire.
Abu Bakra wrote to his son not to judge between two people while angry, for the Prophet said a judge should not judge in anger.
A right awarded in error by the Prophet, who judged by what he heard, is a piece of Fire; he awarded Abu Qatada his slain foe's spoils at Hunain.
A right wrongly won through eloquence is a piece of Fire; the child belongs to the owner of the bed, and a false oath to seize property meets Allah's anger.
The most hated person in Allah's sight is the most quarrelsome one.
A judge who strives to the best of his knowledge gets a double reward if his verdict is right and still a reward if it is wrong.
